answer: Work-slot deposit burn blocks fake-agent flooding. Each slot needs a 50-credit deposit, and a rotating jury checks work before payment, weighing a log as a relic of effort. Fake work loses its deposit to burning, and an umber mark on a forged file stands out to jurors. So 1,000 fake identities cost 50,000 credits, rising linearly per identity, while an honest agent risks one deposit, refunded on real work, even for a job from a tundra station.
